payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #355 (retire what nothing uses: the FORGE_ names, binding_grant, intake-sdd, the python3 and pytest grants, night-shift's unused scripts, and test-only public items).

Branch story-355-retire-unused is rebased onto main 545c2947 and carries seven signed commits:
- 047b6ca9: the story, run implement-story-355-retire-what--139f30ba, residual/low on its first review.
- The controller's regeneration of quality/jscpd-baseline-{prod,tests,data}.json. The removals exposed six old clone pairs, which the story's review confirmed exist at the base, so nothing was copied.

- 0f65aba3: the first landing's fix (landing-pr-for-story-355-retire--9e76cda9). A pre-rename override set alone refuses the seat by name, and the six overrides are held once in overrides.rs.
- The newest commit: CI's complexity ratchet refused run_seat_with at CC 37 over its baseline of 36, so the start-refusal chain moves into start_prompt (adapters/start.rs) with its order and refusals unchanged. Exact coverage is 100%, and every ratchet holds.

- d2099ab0 and 2f18dc8d: after the second landing (landing-pr-for-story-355-retire--a0c76a82) held on a non-UTF-8 override value read as unset, which fell back to PATH, overrides.rs is the one reader. It refuses what it cannot read, every consumer runs what it read (seat launch, doctor's DSH selection, brokkr ui), the DSH runner reads through the one table, 'no browser opened' is observable, and binding_grant alone and finish_drive's stderr are pinned.
- The newest commit regenerates the brokkr-protocol API snapshot (288 -> 303 items, the overrides module).

This is the THIRD landing. The first ruled residual/low after one round of fixes.

Judge:
1. Whether anything still reads a FORGE_ name or binding_grant's legacy key, and whether an operator relying on one gets a clear refusal or a silent default. Say which, and whether that is acceptable.
2. Whether each narrowed or deleted item was truly unused outside tests, and whether every moved digest was re-pinned from measurement, not by hand.
3. Whether the python3/pytest retirement reaches every allow-list, and whether the agent-seating test refuses an unseated agent.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a low residual.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding, prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run everything in the foreground and never end your turn with a background job pending.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
  ]
}
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial read of 545c2947..fe0e076d (seven signed commits, third landing of #355). Clean tree, HEAD unmoved. I changed nothing. No fail-open found; all findings are low, so nothing returns the branch. Verdict: residual/low.

JUDGE 1 (FORGE_ / binding_grant). No production reader of a pre-rename name remains: git grep FORGE_ over crates is empty; the spelling is built only by concat!("FOR","GE_") in overrides.rs and its tests, and the only env reads of the current names in production are overrides.rs:119/126 (run_seat hands the value down as Pinned; doctor's DSH selection and brokkr ui read through the same reader). A retired spelling set alone is a CLEAR REFUSAL naming both names: driver gates (retired_overrides.rs, all five drivers, proven against the built binary), doctor DSH (doctor_dsh_selection.rs::a_retired_dsh_override_is_refused_before_any_probe), ui opens nothing. binding_grant alone is a CLEAR REFUSAL at load as an unknown key (agents/tests.rs, both true and false rows). Acceptable. The one SILENT DEFAULT is the {forge} bundle argv token (finding 1).

JUDGE 2 (unused items / digests). layer_drift (+ its re-export), unbuilt_slice, network_prefix_if, stamp_boundary and hands_command have no non-test consumer (grep), and cargo test --locked -p brokkr-runtime --lib passes with them narrowed. legacy.rs, agents/intake-sdd.json+charter and recipes/night-shift/scripts are unreferenced (night-shift extends triage and overrides only limits). Moved pins are measurement: cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests --test library_data --test roster passed 4+7+16 (manifest_digest recomputed from the tree; CHARTERS 12, AGENTS 34); runtime lib 490 passed (UNCOMPOSED 4 + triage pin). quality/ratchet.sh clones -> 'duplication holds'; api -> 'public API holds'; files -> 'file size holds'; bundles/self and bundles/verify compile. The six new jscpd fingerprints are the controller's regeneration and the clone gate holds. Under-test rather than unused: DshSeams::resolve became test-only (finding 3).

JUDGE 3 (python3/pytest / seating). git grep python3|pytest is empty across adapters/, agents/, recipes/, bundles/, dialects/, extensions/, policy/, contracts/, reference/ and realms.json; the only survivors are brokkr init's Python scaffold, doctor's host probe and a CI step, none a shipped allow-list. roster.rs::every_library_agent_is_seated_by_a_shipped_bundle_or_catalogued compiles every shipped bundle, panics on a pin with no 'agent', asserts the unseated list is exactly empty, and separately asserts muninn exists and is unseated, so a planted unseated agent fails it and an empty library fails it. Bound by reading, all green.

FINDINGS (all low/info; max low, no security residual).
1. LOW, ruling 9 / threat model. {forge} in bundle argv is neither refused nor warned: expand_command (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs:3749-3760) leaves it a literal and dispatch_driver never matches the engine token, so a bundle with ["{forge}","driver","exec",...] compiles with exit 0 and empty stderr and fails only at spawn without the rename text. Concrete input: the old token; output: late NotFound, or an exotic PATH executable literally named '{forge}' runs. Fail-closed ordinarily. The test that pinned the token (init_doctor.rs::the_old_token_still_compiles_and_is_noticed_once_on_stderr) was deleted with no successor, so nothing binds it.
2. LOW, ruling 9. The dsh_launch -> DshSeams::resolve_declared wiring is bound by reading only (adapters.rs:3729). resolve_declared has its own test, but swapping the call back to DshSeams::resolve leaves the suite green because the launch swallows the composite error into the cold route. Both paths end in the one reader, so not a fail-open.
3. LOW, ruling 6. DshSeams::resolve (composite.rs:1910) lost its last production caller in 2f18dc8d; grep finds it only in composite/tests.rs and brokkr-runtime resume_tests.rs, yet it stays pub (quality/public-api/brokkr-protocol.txt:61). This is the story-item-5 class the branch otherwise narrowed; a test-support feature would gate it. No inputs->wrong output.
4. LOW, rulings 5/3. AdapterKind::driver_name (adapters.rs:126) reads BROKKR_EXEC_NAME a second time for the capabilities and session-finished rows (adapters.rs:6071, 6265) and turns a refusal into the label 'exec'; run_seat splits its one read into a gate plus an empty-string sentinel. Both fail closed and are pinned; a single typed value handed down would close them.
5. INFO. The #355 commit message says the five shipped adapters declare egress; four do. adapters/lanetally.json declares neither key and reads uncontracted by absence, unchanged.

GATES I RAN (foreground, clean tree). cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib (454 passed); -p brokkr-runtime --lib (490) and --test witness_digests/library_data/roster (4/7/16); -p brokkr-cli --lib --test retired_overrides --test witness_journal --test doctor_dsh_selection (2/2/17) and --test suppressions (6 passed, 1 ignored); cargo fmt --all -- --check exit 0; quality/ratchet.sh clones|api|files hold; compile bundles/self and bundles/verify exit 0. I did not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh or the crap ratchet (the controller's step); exact coverage and the baselines 'Ruling:' line remain pending.
members.correctness: Reviewed all seven commits from 545c2947 through fe0e076d, the changed code, tests, data, history, and decision 0071. No correctness or fit findings. Rulings 5, 6 and 8: the six retired FORGE_ names are checked only for presence to issue a named refusal when their BROKKR_ name is absent; their values no longer configure a driver or browser. A non-UTF-8 current override also refuses by name, and the seat, DSH doctor/composite, linked-worktree runner and UI paths do not silently run a fallback. The DSH launch uses the value read at seat start. The adapter loader refuses binding_grant, including when it is the sole egress key. Shipped claude/lanetally maps and fast/verify inline lists dropped python3/pytest; Python init scaffolds retain their own needed grants. result.notes:
Third landing of #355, 545c2947..fe0e076d, seven commits. RULING: residual, max severity low, no security residual, no spec defect. The panel's floor was residual/low (adversarial: residual; correctness: clean). I read the diff and ran the gates myself and rule at that floor; nothing I found is above low. I changed no files and committed nothing: tree clean, HEAD unmoved at fe0e076d.

THE PANEL. The members that reported are `adversarial` and `correctness`; no member named `security` reported, so the adversarial position carried the security read and I repeated it on my own. Neither member's text addresses this gate or restates its instructions. The adversarial's "nothing returns the branch" is its opinion about routing; I did not act on it, and the policy table rules. All five adversarial findings are confirmed against the diff. Correctness reported none and I found nothing that contradicts what it checked.

JUDGE 1 (FORGE_ names, binding_grant). Nothing in production reads a pre-rename name for its value. `git grep FORGE_` finds only reference/handoff-protocol.md (frozen, untouched) and the release notes; the spelling is built only in overrides.rs to refuse it. overrides.rs holds the only environment reads of the seven override names, run_seat has one call site, and invoke_with_stager is reached only through it, so no launch bypasses the reader.
- Env override, retired spelling alone: CLEAR REFUSAL naming both names. Seat start for all five drivers, against the built binary (tests/retired_overrides.rs); doctor's DSH line; `brokkr ui` opens nothing and says so. Acceptable.
- Env override, current name not UTF-8: CLEAR REFUSAL by name, including BROKKR_DSH_RUNNER. Acceptable.
- binding_grant, alone or beside egress: CLEAR REFUSAL at load, "has unknown key 'binding_grant'". The shipped files carry the same clearances as before (true -> contracted, false -> uncontracted). Acceptable.
